target.title: fix(config/sessions): narrow reply-session initialization revision to identity fields
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #98672. Users observed `reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:main` errors that broke ongoing sessions until the gateway was restarted. The error came from the guarded reply-session initialization path comparing the full persisted session entry between snapshot and commit.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initialization guard only needs to detect whether another initializer rotated the session (i.e. changed `sessionId`/`sessionFile`). Comparing the entire entry included volatile fields such as `updatedAt`, `lastHeartbeatSentAt`, `contextBudgetStatus`, pending-delivery metadata, etc. These are legitimately mutated by background heartbeat runners, delivery retries, and other gateway activity, so unrelated metadata changes produced false-positive `stale-snapshot` conflicts.

The change narrows `createReplySessionInitializationRevision` to the identity fields `sessionId` and `sessionFile`, and removes the now-unused `projectSessionEntryForPersistenceRevision` helper. A regression test verifies that non-identity metadata changes no longer conflict.

## User Impact

- Sessions no longer fail with `reply session initialization conflicted` when background activity touches session metadata.
- Real session rotations are still detected and retried as before.

## Evidence

- Added regression test `commits reply session initialization despite non-identity metadata changes` in `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.test.ts`.
- `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.test.ts`: 60/60 tests pass.
- `src/config/sessions/` suite: 436/436 tests pass.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-session-lifecycle.test.ts` and `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-session-reset.test.ts`: 17/17 tests pass.
- `tsgo:core` type check passes.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` pass on changed files.
